# LLM inference through Cencori

OpenAI-compatible chat completions. Cencori routes the request to the upstream model and
injects its own credential; the caller never holds an API key.

| route | price | body |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /cencori/v1/chat/completions` | 0.01 USDC | OpenAI chat-completions shape |

## Closed beta: one model

Only `maximo-atlas-1.3` is served. The gateway reads the body before quoting: any other
`model`, a missing one, or a body that is not a JSON object is refused with `400` and
costs nothing. Larger models arrive once the commercial terms are settled.

Include a non-empty `messages` array and set `max_tokens` to **256, 1024 or 4096**.
The body may contain only `model`, `messages`, `max_tokens`, `temperature`, `top_p`,
`stop` and `seed`. Streaming, tools, alternate output-limit fields and multiple
completions are refused before payment. The request body limit is 32 KiB; do not
append a query string to this endpoint.

Text only. Each message carries only `role`, `content` and an optional `name`. Its
`content` is a string, or an array of `{"type": "text", "text": "..."}` parts. Image,
audio and file parts are refused before payment.

Of the body, that is all the gateway checks before quoting: which fields are present,
the values of `model` and `max_tokens`, and that every message is text. It does not
check roles, order or any other value. A request with no `messages`, or an empty array,
is quoted and charged like any other, and what Cencori makes of it arrives after
payment.

```json
{
  "model": "maximo-atlas-1.3",
  "max_tokens": 256,
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Summarise this in one line: ..."}]
}
```

## Flat price per completion

One call, one price, whatever the response length. The price does not vary with tokens,
so there is nothing to reconcile afterwards. Choose one of the three supported output
limits with `max_tokens`; that choice does not change what you pay.

This is deliberate. x402 settles the amount signed into the EIP-3009 authorisation, so a
"pay up to X, settle actual usage" flow is not expressible today (see `cpay#21`). A flat
price is honest about that rather than implying metering that does not happen.

The gateway bounds the request size and output limit before quoting. Its upstream
allowance, when configured, retains a conservative per-call reserve; provider credit
and project spending limits are maintained by the operator.

## Buying it

```text
buy_pay_quote
  url:    https://gateway.usebuy.ai/cencori/v1/chat/completions
  method: POST
  headers: {"content-type":"application/json"}
  body:   "{\"model\":\"maximo-atlas-1.3\",\"max_tokens\":256,\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"hi\"}]}"
```

Then `buy_curl` with the same url, method and body, and `maxAmount` from the quote.

## What comes back

The upstream OpenAI-compatible response: `choices[0].message.content`, plus `usage` with
prompt, completion and total tokens. Report the content to the user; `usage` is
informational only and does not affect the price paid.

## Failures

Refused before payment, so they cost nothing and carry no `X-PAYMENT-RESPONSE`:

- `400` for a field outside the list above, a missing or unsupported `model` or
  `max_tokens`, a query string, a body that is not a JSON object, or a message
  that is not text (an image, audio or file part, or a key other than `role`,
  `content` and `name`).
- `405` for a paid request with any method but `POST`, `413` for a body over 32 KiB. An
  unpaid request with no body, by `POST`, `GET` or `HEAD`, gets the `402` with the price.
- `429` from the gateway's own rate limit. Wait for `Retry-After`, then retry.
- `503` with `paymentSettled: false` when the upstream allowance is spent.

A failure after settlement was paid for, and carries an `X-PAYMENT-RESPONSE` receipt:

- any status Cencori itself returns, its own `400`, `429` or `5xx` included;
- `504` from the gateway when Cencori has not finished within 180 seconds, and `502`
  when its response could not be relayed.

That header, not the status, says whether a call was charged. Check for it before
retrying a failure: if it is there, a retry signs a new authorisation and is charged
again. When the response was lost or is a `500`, run `buy receipts --resolve` before
doing anything else.

Some of those paid failures are refunded. When a call settled and you got no
completion, because of the gateway's `504` or `502`, a Cencori `5xx`, or a Cencori
`401`, `402`, `403` or `429` (the gateway's own credential or credit failing, not your
request), the gateway records a refund owed to the paying address, keyed by the
settlement transaction in the receipt. An operator sends it back in the same token
and amount. You do not need to ask, and a retry is charged on its own. A Cencori `400`
or other `4xx` comes from the request and is not refunded, and neither is a call you
abandoned before it answered. Keep the receipt's transaction hash; it identifies the
refund.
